_comment: THE LEVER TABLE. The matrix is GENERATED from this file, so the set of levers under test is a
reviewable artefact rather than a number somebody remembers. Add a row and the matrix grows by
construction; there is no second place to edit.
FIELDS, and why each one is mandatory:
key       the runtime config key, exactly as read by the engine.
baseline  the value the perf harness runs by default. ASSERTED against
harness/storage-perf/starbound.config before every leg -- a lever whose baseline has
drifted from the harness is measuring something nobody declared.
off       the value that REVERTS THE OPTIMISATION, i.e. restores the behaviour that existed
before the lever was written. null is not a placeholder: the runner REFUSES a table
with a null off-value, because guessing it is how an A/B measures nothing.
witness   the metric key the lever EXISTS TO MOVE. This is the load-bearing field. On
2026-08-04 an adaptive-border A/B ran with the lever off on BOTH legs and produced a
full table of plausible deltas; the tell was that lighting.calc.cells was identical
across the legs, and nothing in the tooling objected. The runner now objects: if the
witness does not move between baseline and off, the leg is VOID, not a result.
changesOutput  true when the two legs do not render the same image. Such a lever's cost delta
is not a free win and may not be quoted as one without saying what was traded.
why       what the lever does, in one line. Not narration -- it is what a reader needs to judge
whether the witness is the right witness.
EVERY off-VALUE BELOW WAS READ OUT OF THE CODE, NOT REMEMBERED. Two would have been wrong from
memory, and both would have silently produced a full matrix of artefacts:
* parallaxRefreshInterval=0 IS NOT 'off'. 0 is the ADAPTIVE sentinel, resolved to a per-scene N
before any clamp (StarBackdropPass.cpp: '0 = ADAPTIVE (default), 1 = off/direct, >1 = manual').
The harness baseline therefore runs the parallax cache ON. Setting it to 0 as the 'off' leg
would have compared the cache against itself.
* envRefreshInterval clamps anything <1 up to 1, and the cache only engages at >1. So 0 and 1
are the same behaviour, and 1 -- not 0 -- is the off-value.
The two keys look like the same quantity, share a type, and are read three lines apart. They are
not on a shared scale.

levers.why: Env cache: reuse the composed environment for N frames. At N=1 the cache does not engage at all (envCacheActive is interval>1), so the skip counter must fall to zero on the off leg. Output differs by BOUNDED STALENESS, not quality: a reused frame shows content up to N-1 frames old.

Parallax cache. Baseline 0 is ADAPTIVE -- the engine derives N per scene from layer drift rate, snapped to {1,2,4,8,16}. 1 is off/direct. The skip counter must fall to zero on the off leg. Bounded staleness as above, plus a documented sub-ULP quantisation from premultiplied blending.

Reuse the previous lightmap on calm frames instead of recomputing every frame. Off is a byte-identical every-frame recompute, so the skip counter must fall to zero. On, a calm frame shows a lightmap up to lightingTemporalFloorMs old.

Cache built drawables across frames instead of rebuilding per call. Off takes the full-rebuild path, so the cached-parts counter must fall to zero. Byte-identity is verified by a dedicated shadowCompare diagnostic, modulo a documented sub-ULP float-ordering tolerance on position.

_gapsComment: LEVERS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE MATRIX, AND WHY. Recorded here rather than omitted silently,
because a matrix that quietly covers half the levers reads exactly like one that covers them all.
Every entry below is the SAME defect: the lever has no registered counter, so nothing in telemetry
can say whether it ENGAGED. Asserting on its timer instead would assert the RESULT and call it the
cause -- which is the confusion this whole campaign exists to end. Each gap closes by registering
one counter at the lever's own branch; none needs a design.
Note the shape: the two levers with the largest measured wins in this project's history are both
in here. The instrument is weakest exactly where the stakes are highest.

gaps.reason: No counter exists. The lever is byte-identical by construction and its entire effect is stall cost, so no count differs between the arms. This is the biggest single GPU win the project has measured (74-81% of the GPU frame at the Director's bases), and it is currently the least provable.
gaps.closes: register a counter of orphaned buffer writes at the branch in StarRenderer_opengl.cpp

gaps.reason: No counter exists. The branch at StarWorldClient.cpp:2377 selects the stable-grid path or the original direct gather, and neither arm records anything. The key is also read via get(...).optBool() rather than getOrDefault, so it is outside the config-lint declaration gate as well.
gaps.closes: register a gather cache-hit counter at the branch

gaps.reason: No script.* metric is registered anywhere in the telemetry corpus, so there is nothing to witness. The off path is documented as the original code path byte for byte.
gaps.closes: register a proto-cache hit/miss counter in StarLuaRoot

gaps.reason: The merged arm defers the env compose and the standalone arm calls composeEnvStandalone, so the two arms genuinely differ -- but render.pass.parallax.compose.gpu_us fires in both, so its count does not witness which arm ran. Proven algebraically byte-identical.
gaps.closes: register a counter on the standalone-compose branch in StarBackdropPass.cpp

_excludedComment: NOT LEVERS, and excluded for reasons that are not gaps:
monochromeLighting -- these CHANGE RENDERED OUTPUT. Their cost delta is a trade, not a win, and
quoting one as a free saving would be false. lightingGpu additionally has NO bit-identity oracle
against the CPU path (lightingGpuShadowCompare is documented as permanently red for an unrelated
reason: it can detect a change but cannot certify identity), and toggling it while
lightingWorldUpscale stays pinned at 2 gives the world shader a UV scale that does not match the
CPU lightmap it is sampling -- a coordinate mismatch, not a quality difference.
lightingGpuSpreadIterations -- hybrid. Below the converged value it changes pixels (8.8% differ
at 32 vs 48); at or above it is cost-only. The harness pins exactly 48, the boundary, so there is
no headroom to lower it without corrupting the comparison.
tuning parameters of a lever already in the table, not independent on/off switches.
vaoBake -- DEAD. Zero readers in source/; #129 reverted the lever it named and the key survived in
the pinned harness config controlling nothing. config-lint cannot see it: that gate polices
undeclared getOrDefault reads, and a key declared nowhere and read nowhere is invisible to it.
